title: Kaia vs Gong: Which Fits Your Sales Team?
summary: Kaia vs Gong is usually a category confusion: one helps reps live inside Outreach, the other analyses calls afterwards. Here is how to choose.
body_markdown:
Teams searching for Kaia vs Gong are usually comparing two tools that solve different problems: Kaia helps a rep during a meeting, Gong tells the team what happened after it. Once you see that, the choice gets much simpler, and for many teams the honest answer is that the two are not substitutes at all.


## 01


Why the comparison keeps coming up


Both tools join your sales calls. Both transcribe. Both put the word AI near the word revenue. So they land on the same shortlists, and buyers assume they compete.


They mostly do not. Kaia and Gong sit at different points in the life of a call, serve different people, and are bought in different ways. Comparing them feature by feature without seeing that leads to the wrong purchase, usually an expensive one.


## 02


What is Outreach Kaia?


Kaia is the meeting assistant inside Outreach, the sales execution platform. It joins meetings booked through Outreach, transcribes them live, and shows the rep content cards in real time. When a prospect mentions a competitor or asks about a feature, a card appears with the talking points your admin loaded for that trigger. Kaia also captures action items and writes summaries back into Outreach workflows.


Two things follow from that design. First, Kaia is a platform feature, not a standalone product. You get it because you run Outreach; you cannot buy it alone. Second, its live help is only as good as the cards someone in your organisation has configured and kept current. An empty or stale card library means a quiet Kaia.


If your team is on Outreach already, Kaia is worth switching on. If not, the question is moot, and you should be reading a list of[Outreach Kaia alternatives](https://www.caretta.so/blog/outreach-kaia-alternatives) instead.


## 03


What is Gong?


Gong is the best-known conversation intelligence platform, and it earned that position. It records and transcribes calls across the whole team, then analyses them: talk ratios, topics, questions asked, competitor mentions, next steps. Managers use it to coach reps against real calls instead of hearsay. RevOps uses its revenue intelligence layer to spot deals going quiet and forecast from what buyers actually said.


Gong's centre of gravity is after the call. A rep can search past calls and read summaries, but the product is built for the people reviewing conversations at scale: managers, enablement, and RevOps. It has become the default answer for call review the way a CRM is the default answer for pipeline records.


What Gong does not do is help the rep in the moment. It will tell you on Tuesday that Monday's demo went off the rails at minute twelve. It will not say anything at minute twelve.


## 04


Kaia vs Gong: how do they actually differ?


Dimension Outreach Kaia Gong


When it helps During the meeting After the call


What you buy A feature of the Outreach platform A standalone conversation and revenue intelligence platform


Primary user The rep in the meeting Managers, enablement, RevOps


Knowledge source Content cards an admin configures The growing corpus of your recorded calls


Strongest at Live prompts and action capture inside Outreach meetings Coaching, deal visibility, searchable call history at scale


Weakest at Anything outside Outreach; card upkeep falls on admins Helping a rep while the call is still happening


The rows matter more than the logos. If your problem lives in the left half of the table (reps freezing on objections, answers arriving a day late), you need in-meeting help. If it lives in the right half (no visibility into calls, coaching by anecdote, forecasts built on vibes), you need conversation intelligence.


## 05


Which one should your team choose?


Start from your situation, then pick the tool.


1. **You run Outreach and reps need live support.** Turn Kaia on. It is already in the platform you pay for, and the main cost is the admin time to build and maintain good cards.
2. **You need coaching and deal visibility at scale.** Gong, regardless of which sequencer you use. Nothing in Kaia replaces a proper call corpus with analysis on top.
3. **You have budget for both problems.** Plenty of teams run Outreach and Gong side by side: Kaia for the live meeting, Gong for review and pipeline. The vs in this pairing is a budgeting question, not a feature bake-off.
4. **You do not run Outreach.** Kaia drops out of the running entirely. Compare Gong against standalone meeting assistants on their own merits.
5. **You want live coaching but Gong-style review is not the gap.** Post-call platforms are heavy if the real problem is what happens mid-call; there is a growing set of[alternatives focused on real-time coaching](https://www.caretta.so/blog/gong-alternatives-real-time-coaching) .


Be honest about the second case in particular. If managers cannot answer basic questions about what happens on calls, no amount of live assistance fixes that. Review at scale is Gong's job and it does it well.


## 06


When neither tool answers the real question


There is a third need hiding inside many Kaia vs Gong searches: reps want accurate answers from the organisation's own knowledge while the prospect is still on the line. Which security certifications do we hold? How did we handle this objection the last three times? What does our integration with their stack actually support?


Kaia can only surface what an admin wrote into a card in advance. Gong can answer from past calls, but after the meeting. If live answers drawn from your docs, CRM, and call history are the actual gap, look at a realtime copilot such as[Caretta](https://www.caretta.so/product) , which listens to the conversation and pulls answers from that knowledge during the meeting rather than requiring anyone to script cards up front.


That is a different category again. Naming the gap precisely is most of the work of choosing.


## 07


The short version


Kaia is an in-meeting assistant you already own if you run Outreach. Gong is the standard for understanding calls after they happen. Pick by where your problem sits in the life of a call, expect that mature teams often end up with both, and reserve the word alternative for tools that solve the same problem, which these two mostly do not.
